comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
If you have SWAG installed, Questing Bots’s spawn system will be disabled; only SWAG/DONUTS will manage spawning. The only reason the Questing Bots endpoint appears instead of the EFT one is because it changes the PScav conversion chance with every request. Otherwise, it just passes the data right through.

If you can repeatably make Scav spawn rates change when having Questing Bots installed vs. uninstalled, feel free to post a link to a ZIP with the following files, and I’ll take a look:

  • LogOutput.log in BepInEx\
  • Everything in Logs\
  • The most recent server log in user\logs\

comments.author: DanW

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
You’re correct, these errors are not caused by Questing Bots.

Questing Bots reroute the bot-generation request so it can control the PScav conversion chance for it, but otherwise it doesn’t make any changes. Likely this is caused by another mod that changes bot loadouts or modifies items/weapons in the game. I’m not too experienced with mods that make those types of changes, so without knowing any better my suggestion is to remove them until the problem stops. It’ll likely take some experimentation to figure it out. Good luck!

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html: BSG’s approach with streets and Ground Zero is to keep spawning Scavs until the bot cap is reached, and this often prevents new PMC’s from spawning in. The Questing Bots advanced spawning system “tricks” EFT into thinking that the PMC’s and PScavs it spawns are human players and therefore don’t count toward the bot cap. This allows me much better control over spawn times.

comments.author: e-dog
comments.body_html:
To anybody having this issue too, know that this can only be resolved by changing the .dll file (aka the one who goes into the plugin folder). Changing the package.json file in the user/mods folder doesn’t do anything, as far as I know.

You’ll have to “decompile” the .dll file using dnSpy.
Here’s a quick guide on how to do it:

1. Download dnSpy and open the .dll file from the plugins folder.
2. Once opened, go into “SPTQuestingBots” by clicking on it,
3. Then to “SPTQuestingBots.dll”,
4. Then to “SPTQuestingBots” but in yellow,
5. Then to “QuestingBotsPlugin”,
6. Then to “Awake()”.
7. Now, once opened, there should be a bunch of code to your left. Just right-click on any of it, and click on “Edit IL Instructions”.
8. Line 1 should be “3.8.0.0”, just change that to “0.0.0.0”.
9. Click on OK at the bottom right, then click on Save All button in the toolbar at the top (or press Ctrl + Shift + S)
10. A window will pop up. Edit “Filename” to where you want to put the .dll file (either the plugin folder directly, or an intermediary folder)
10.5. Overwrite the .dll file (if you save the new .dll file into the plugin folder directly)
11. Click on the OK of that pop-up.
12. If you saved the .dll file to an intermediary folder, replace the old .dll file with new one.

And that should be it! Enjoy your mod!

*I don’t know if the mod works even if the version check fails, it probably still does.
And if it does, welp, that’s 2 hours of my left I won’t ever get back researching this shit.

And no, I will not share my .dll file, edit the file yourself.*

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
There have been a lot of pathing issues since BSG updated to 0.14.x, so this could be a symptom of that.

It’s really difficult to say what happened without seeing it occur live. At the very least, you’d need to watch the Questing Bots’s bot overlays to see what each bot in the group was doing. Also, two things to keep in mind are:

1) Bots WILL get stuck, so as long as this doesn’t occur frequently, we have to accept it

2) Bots don’t need to exactly replicate human behavior. The real objective of this mod is to have bots move around the map in a somewhat plausible manner while interacting with their environment (looting, unlocking doors, etc.) along the way. If they stick around one location doing seemingly nothing for a few minutes, that’s not super unrealistic. If you weren’t using debugging tools, you probably wouldn’t notice.

fraction_of_max_players_vs_raidET reduces the lobby size if you spawn in late as a Scav. comments.author: CodyL
comments.body_html:
I’m not the mod author, but I think this is how it works.

Bot cap refers to AI scavs and presumably bosses, “max_alive_bots” refers to PMCs and PScavs.

Total bot cap is calculated as max_alive_bots + bot cap + offset. In your case 14 + 17 + -5 = 26.

Try this:

“advanced_eft_bot_count_management”: { “enabled”: true, “use_EFT_bot_caps”: true, “only_decrease_bot_caps”: false, “bot_cap_adjustments”: { // … “interchange”: -5, // … } } // Handled by “advanced_eft_bot_count_management”. “bot_cap_adjustments” : { “enabled”: false // … } “max_alive_bots”: { // … “interchange”: 14 // … } Also, you might struggle to reach the total bot cap with such a high “max_alive_bots” value, as AI scavs seem to repopulate much faster than PScavs. From my understanding lowering this value reduces the number of PMCs/PScavs which can exist simultaneously, not the overall number of PMCs per raid.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
If you increase the values of bot_spawns.max_alive_bots to match the maximum player count for each map (minus one, because you count as one of them), all of the PMC’s will spawn at the beginning of the raid. However, please keep in mind that this will have a performance impact. Factory and Labs are set up this way by default, and the other maps have lower limits for performance reasons.

The spawning system purposely makes bots spawn in remote areas to spread out the action. This is both for performance reasons and so the majority of the raid doesn’t feel dead compared to the first 5-10 min. There isn’t a way to change this behavior. However, allowing more PMC’s to spawn at the beginning of the raid will inherently mean that some will spawn closer to you.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
CodyL is correct. When you have bot_spawns.advanced_eft_bot_count_management.enabled=true (which is the default setting), EFT only respects your bot cap for Scavs and bosses. PMC’s and PScavs will be allowed to exceed the bot cap, and they have their own cap defined by bot_spawns.max_alive_bots.

You should be able to do what CodyL suggested and adjust bot_spawns.advanced_eft_bot_count_management.bot_cap_adjustments, but this is ONLY used when bot_spawns.advanced_eft_bot_count_management.use_EFT_bot_caps=true. That’s why you’re not seeing any effect by changing it. If that setting is enabled, you’ll see the bot caps displayed in the server when you start it, so you can make adjustments accordingly based on your bot_spawns.max_alive_bots settings.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
The changes you made will only work on maps that use BSG’s “new” spawning system. Their “new” spawning system regularly keeps spawning Scavs until the bot cap is reached, and it checks if they’re allowed to spawn every ~15 seconds. In contrast, BSG’s “old” system has predefined bot waves, and each wave has ranges for the time it will spawn and the number of bots that will spawn in it.

In SPT 3.8.x, all maps use the “new” spawning system except Factory and Reserve. Therefore, you’ll notice that bots will spawn much slower on those maps compared to all of the others.

There is a flag that can be changed for each map to toggle between the spawning systems, but I’ve never tried changing it. I’m not sure what will happen.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html: Basically, advanced_eft_bot_count_management and bot_cap_adjustments aren’t intended to be enabled at the same time. You can think of bot_cap_adjustments as Questing Bots’s old spawning system and advanced_eft_bot_count_management as its new one. max_additional_bots defines the limit that the bot cap for each map is allowed to be increased when add_max_players_to_bot_cap=true. By default, it’s 5, which means that if the bot cap for a map is 20, and the lobby size for it is 10 players, the bot cap will be increased to 25 instead of 30. Regardless of this setting, max_total_bots still defines the upper limit for the bot cap if bot_cap_adjustments.enabled=true.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
You can experiment with them, but I’ve found that lower is generally better. Doubling those values is a pretty significant change.

“Players” is actually a misnomer; the code checks for proximity to any player or bot in the raid. comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
Yes, bot_spawns.pmcs.fraction_of_max_players is purposely omitted from the config because changing it will make your raids deviate from the live-like experience I’m trying to achieve. However, there’s no problem with manually adding it. It scales the PMC lobby size for the map. For example, normally Customs will allow 10-12 PMC’s, and if you change that value to 1.5, it will then allow 15-18 PMC’s.

Yes, the bot cap affects all bot types except the PMC’s and PScavs generated by this mod (if advanced_eft_bot_count_management is enabled). The SPT bot caps are based on EFT’s bot caps for each map, but the SPT developers manually modify them. Some maps are increased to allow PMC’s to spawn in addition to normal Scavs, and some maps are decreased (namely Streets) for performance. use_EFT_bot_caps discards SPT’s bot caps and uses BSG’s values for them instead. You can see the changes made when the server starts.

The “from humans” slider sets the distance within which all bots are active from human players (i.e. you). The “from questing bots” slider sets the distance within which all bots are active from bots that are allowed to quest per this mod’s config. comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
The total number of PMC’s that can spawn is determined by the EFT lobby size for the map (i.e. 10-12 for Customs). You can add a “hidden” field, fraction_of_max_players, to bot_spawns.pmcs to scale the lobby sizes. You can reference bot_spawns.player_scavs.fraction_of_max_players as an example.

There is no spawn delay for new PMC’s to spawn, but there is a minimum time for each PScav. The PScav minimum spawn times are determined algorithmically using the SPT raid-delay settings for Scav raids for each map. You can see them in the bepinex console just as the raid is about to begin. The only way to change this is by altering the SPT raid-delay settings.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
The “bot counts” are used by EFT spawns, which are Scavs and bosses. EFT will regularly spawn bots to try and approach (or reach) that total number during the raid. It won’t spawn bots immediately as the raid starts; it will be more gradual. PMC’s and player Scavs spawned by this mod do not count toward that limit. Instead, the maximum total number of PMC’s and player Scavs is specified by the bot_spawns.max_alive_bots values in config.json. The total number bot bots allowed on the map at any given time is the sum of EFT’s bot cap (“SPT bot counts” shown in the server messages) and the bot_spawns.max_alive_bots value for the map.

As you said, after waiting for “BotSpawnPeriodCheck” seconds, EFT will spawn more bots if it determines it should. I’m not sure how its algorithm works.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
max_total_bots and pretty much the whole bot_cap_adjustments section is obsolete, and I should remove it. I left it in for a while because I didn’t know how well my “new” spawn system would work, but that was many months ago. I would leave that section disabled (as it is by default).

As you said, max_alive_bots controls the maximum number of PMC’s and PScav’s on the map. However, the total number of PMC’s is still limited by the lobby size for the map (and you count as one of them). That’s why for Factory, you’ll never have more than 5 PMC’s spawn. For PScav’s, there is also a spawn schedule for each of them that’s created dynamically (defining the earliest they can spawn). The lobby size for PScavs is also increased by 1.5X by default using the fraction_of_max_players config setting. You can copy that setting over to the pmcs section if you want to increase the lobby size for them too.

For all other bots (Scavs and bosses), EFT manages everything using whatever bot caps you apply. By default, Questing Bots changes bot caps to closely match live EFT’s (the use_EFT_bot_caps setting), but streets is slightly reduced due to performance concerns.

What are you trying to accomplish? You’ve changed so much in the config file that it’s a bit hard to understand what’s happening.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
No, if you want all PMC’s to spawn at the beginning of the raid, you’ll want to set the bot_spawns.max_alive_bots values to match the maximum lobby sizes for each map (minus one because you count as a PMC). For example, the lobby size for Customs is 10-12 players, so you would set “bigmap” to 11 for this setting.

The reasons this isn’t already done are:

  • This mod makes PMC and PScav spawns ignore the bot cap for the map, so allowing all PMC’s to spawn at the beginning of the raid can have a performance impact.
  • If all PMC’s spawn at the beginning of the raid, they tend to get into lots of early fights and die off quickly. Not only does this cause raids to be “dead” after the first 10-20 min, it’s not realistic (besides Factory and Labs) because some human players in raids are actively avoiding combat.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
For Lighthouse, your max_alive_bots setting is 9, which means Questing Bots will only allow 9 PMC’s or PScavs to be alive at the same time. To cap the total bots on the map at 20, that means you need to limit the EFT bot spawns to 11. By default, the EFT bot cap for Lighthouse is 17 (which this mod respects by default). Therefore, you need to set the value for Lighthouse in bot_cap_adjustments to -6 (11 - 17 = -6), which you current have at 4.

Keep in mind that 11 is a low EFT bot cap for Lighhouse, so you may need to experiment with the max_initial_rogues setting or you may see very few Scav spawns.

Furthermore, I would highly recommend setting bot_spawns.bot_cap_adjustments.enabled to false. That section is now obsolete and will be removed when I update this mod for SPT 3.10.

Finally, I noticed that you added the fraction_of_max_players field for PMC’s and set it to 5. That will multiply the max lobby size by 5, which means you can have up to 60 PMC’s spawn during a raid (although only 9 can be alive at the same time per your max_alive_bots setting). I’m not sure if that was intentional.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
How did you get -17 for the bot cap adjustment? The EFT cap is 0 (which I assume is no cap), so setting it to 3 should give you a maximum of 3 Scavs.

However, please keep in mind that:

  • These are bot caps, not target bot counts. Sometimes the actual bot counts will be lower.
  • EFT allows some bot spawns to ignore bot caps (namely some boss groups)
  • It’s not possible to have a global target or cap for all bots; they’re completely separate systems.

The objective of the spawning system in this mod is to mimic live EFT. It’s not meant to be a SWAGNUTS replacement.

comments.body_html:
Also, thats just not enough PMCs. With BSP I am able to set exactly how many I want to spawn and they ALL spawn at the start of the raid.

Need a setting to set exact PMC count and have them all spawn at the start of raid. I just dont like them being able to come throughout the raid. Raids feel far too calm with only 7ish PMCs running around at the start.

Number of PMCs (and player scavs spawned by Questing Bots) on map are defined under max\_alive\_bots Bump them up a bit and you’ll have more initial spawn of PMCs. The spawn system tries to fill this spawn cap and maintain it throughout the raid by taking PMC bots from the “bucket”. Once the PMC bucket is exausted, no more PMC spawn can happen. The system then starting filling the cap by spawning player scavs using the pscav bucket.

By default the PMC bucket size is the room size of the map. Note this part of the readme.

For example, Customs allows 10-12 players, but Questing Bots only allows 7 to be on the map at the same time by default. That means 7 PMC’s will spawn immediately as the raid starts, and as some of them die others will spawn to replace them.

10-12 here is the bucket size, while 7 is the default max_alive_bots. Bucket size is defined by fraction\_of\_max\_players as a multiplier of the official room size of each map.

  • If you want PMCs only spawn at the beginning of the raid you need to increase max_alive_bots so that it can accommodate the initial spawn. Then adjust the actual number of PMCs by increasing or decreasing the fraction_of_max_players multiplier if needed.
  • If you want to see PMCs spawn through the entire raid, max_alive_bots need to be relative small compared to the actual bucket size so that bots can trickle in as existing bots die off.

comments.body_html:
Hi I’m trying to achieve something similar to you in terms of performance whilst having a lively, difficult raids. I noticed on lighthouse, and interchange (and I’m assuming streets too, as infamous as it is, though I haven’t tried), my bot spawns go upwards of 25 and sometimes over 30. This, among other things, results in a CPU bottleneck even with a CPU that is supposed to somewhat good at this game. (specs below)

This bottleneck, I’ve found, isn’t only due to the bot spawns as I DO have all the heaviest hitters in terms on AI logic modded into my game with no performance tweaks whatsoever (these being SAIN, Questing bots, That’s Lit (and looting bots to an extent)).

Like you I don’t the like idea of limiting AI because I do feel that would make things a bit dead for me, and make sniping unfair as I only notice performance increases at AI limiting of 300M.

So basically I wanted more performance whilst keeping the raid lively and not too different from either the default mod options or a “live-like” experience

Unfortunately optimizations like the boot config, using process lasso, disabling SMT, and even undervolting my CPU did not do much to assuage my performance issues.

This left me with a few options that I can think of:

1) Lessen the amount of bots

2) Tweak the AI Logic mods with performance tweaks

3) Use frame generation with Lossless scaling/AFMF2 (since I’m on AMD)

I’ve actually tried lessening the amount of bots but on maps like lighthouse, for some reason, even with around 18 bots my cpu struggles (I notice my GPU not being fully utilized, I notice low fps, and I notice high CPU usage on single threads)

If ever I was going to lessen bots, I’d want to have atleast 20 bots running but, I noticed very little performance gain between 16 to 20 bots and 25 to 30 bots.

This made me believe it was the AI logic that really caused performance issues.

With that some tweaks I’ve tried so far (with their corresponding performance gain/loss for me) are as following ;

1. SAIN - Using Vanilla Scavs/Bosses including goons (Little to no noticeable performance gain. However ,since it’s closer to live-like to have braindead Scavs, I keep vanilla scavs hoping that it helps my performance even just a little bit)

2. SAIN - Performance mode (Noticeable performance gain, however I turned it off for now as I want my bots to still be as difficult as can be)

3. That’s Lit - Disabling light tweaks (Incredible performance gain. I noticed this was probably the heaviest hitter contributing to my CPU bottleneck, however once again I like having it on so for now I’ve kept it on)

4. That’s Lit - Only affects PMCs (noticeable but not great performance gain. I like this settings because it falls in line with keeping my game a bit more “live like” only affecting PMCs whilst giving me somewhat of a performance increase.)

5. Questing bots - AI limiting for bots that are questing - including rogues (noticeable but not great performance gain. I noticed on maps like lighthouse, there is some improvement, however not to my satisfaction)

6. Frame gen - this helped me the most. LS provides the smoothest looking image (even when recording), however the input latency makes it unplayable for me. AFMF2 is a bit less smooth, however the input latency is near unnoticeable.

So far those are the only tweaks I’ve tried, however a few things that I do plan to do and test are;

1. Looting Bots - Tweak looting bots to make it so bots only loot what they can see, and lower their loot radius

2. Questing Bots - tweak the bot spawn config to limit bots to at max 22, having around 10 to 12 PMCs with, maybe 5 scavs at max that respawn every time 1 is killed, and the rest for bosses. For this I need to play around with the config of this mod a bit.

I’ll keep thinking of ways to improve performance, however so far that’s just what I’ve tried and plan to try.

To give a possible answer to your questions though:

I would suggest reducing the overall bot count by 1/3 and increasing the waves at which PMCs/ Player scavs spawn

In my testing, reducing the bot_cap_adjustments doesn’t mess with the boss spawns. For assurance I turn on the “spawn initial bosses first” in the config to give them priority.

R7 5700x3D

RX 7600

DDR4 3200 GB

NVME M2 SSD

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html: The “suspicious” time makes them pause their questing for a random time between the min and max values when they hear enemy footsteps or gunshots. The max values are used so they don’t remain “suspicious” for a long period of time and never actually quest. The reason this value is higher on some maps is because smaller maps tend to have bots closer together, meaning they’re more likely to have events make them “suspicious” continuously throughout the raid. comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
Yes, those values are in seconds.

I think there are a few things to clarify about this:

  • I think you’re confusing the min/max values with the overall max values per map. The shorter min/max values are used per instance of bots hearing suspicious noises. In contrast, the overall max values are the maximum total time that bots can remain in a suspicious state (which resets after the cooldown time). This would be the result of many “suspicious” instances being chained together (i.e. them hearing a long fight on the other side of a wall).
  • The intention isn’t for them to freeze and do nothing; it’s simply for them not to quest. The actual logic they use while being suspicious depends on the bot type and the mods you’re using (namely SAIN).
  • The reason for the “suspicious” state being added is that when bots quest, they are unable to engage in combat. Therefore, I needed to monitor various stimuli to detect when questing should be disabled to allow them to react. The “suspicious” state was implemented because previous checks were only able to consider situations where bots were damaged or an enemy was visible to them. Until recently, Rogues were the only bot type that reacted to noises.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
There are no quests that make bots run for gunshots. That’s mostly accomplished via SAIN.

If you want to increase the chance of bots selecting specific quests, you can increase their “desirability” ratings in the JSON file for the corresponding map. Performance will be worse when they calculate longer paths, but ideally this should only happen as they begin heading towards it (either initially or after resuming from doing something else). If they can’t find a complete path, they will try calculating the path again every 5 seconds (by default).

The quest-selection algorithm for bots is a bit complicated, but the “desirability” of the quest and the bot’s distance to it are the primary factors.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
If you’re using the Questing Bots spawning system, the PMC conversion chances need to be kept at 0% at all times for it to work correctly. Questing Bots changes them to 0% when the client loads. If they don’t remain at 0% after that, you’ll see those errors because another mod is overriding those changes.

If SVM sets the conversion chances when the server starts and doesn’t touch them again, that shouldn’t cause those errors. If SVM changes them regularly, that would cause problems and explains why you’re seeing those errors.

Are you using Realism? That’s the most common cause of these errors. Updating both Questing Bots and Realism to their latest versions should fix it.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
1. Bots automatically detect nearby locked doors when they can’t form a complete path to their objective. There’s only a chance they’ll have the key to unlock it, and if they don’t, they give up and choose another quest. There is a way to instruct them to specifically unlock certain doors, but it’s tedious and I don’t recommend it - especially for more than a small number of quests. Keycard doors are treated the same as normal locked doors.
  2. Questing Bots invokes SAIN to make bots extract. SAIN ignores extract requirements because some maps have few (if any) extracts that don’t have restrictions. We determined it would be too complicated to change bot inventories to get them to abide by those restrictions, and that may cause unrealistic behavior by itself.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
That change will allow 15 PMC’s to be alive on each map at the same time. However, the PMC limit for each map is defined by its lobby size. Therefore, you’ll have to change it. There are two ways of doing this:

  1. Use another mod (I’m not sure which) to increase the minimum lobby size of each map to 15 or higher
  2. Add another field named fraction_of_max_players in the pmcs section and set it to 2. You can see this field in the player_scavs section for reference. That will double the lobby size for all maps, which is the minimum adjustment needed. The PMC limit for Factory is 8, and you’re counted as a PMC, so (15 + 1) / 8 = 2.

I should also mention that the objective of the Questing Bots spawning system is to replicate live Tarkov. It was never intended to be highly customizable.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
Yes, SPT caps in 3.11 are now equal to EFT’s caps. You can adjust them using the bot_spawns.bot_cap_adjustments.map_specific_adjustments config.json setting. Whenever an adjustment is made, you’ll see a corresponding server message about it.

Also, maintaining a 1:1 Scav:PMC ratio will be very challenging because Questing Bots and EFT use very different approaches to spawning bots. While your maximum bots might be equal, the actual bots on the map will probably not match.

comments.author: DanW
comments.body_html:
Questing Bots will only spawn a fixed number of PMC’s in a raid (approximately the max player lobby size for the map); it won’t spawn an unlimited amount of them. The reason it staggers PMC spawns is for performance. If you didn’t use debugging tools, you probably wouldn’t notice the delayed spawns. It would just simulate some players be stealthy and keeping a low profile early in the raid.

If you only want one wave of PMC spawns, you’ll need to experiment with the following configuration settings:

  • max_alive_bots: Set this to one less than the max player lobby size for each map. For example, Customs has a lobby size of 10-12 players, so you’d want to max_alive_bots to be 11 for this map (because you count as a PMC). After doing this, all PMC’s will spawn during the first wave, and unless the map is too crowded to spawn all of them at once, none should spawn for the remainder of the raid.
  • map_specific_adjustments: If the performance impact of increasing max_alive_bots is too severe, you can compensate by reducing the number of other bots (namely Scavs) that can spawn using this setting. A negative number will reduce the bot cap for the map. I would not recommend reducing each map by more than -6 for large maps and -3 for small maps or the bot-type imbalance will be noticeable.
